turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome. What brings you into the clinic today?
turns.patient_response: Well, I guess I'm here because... honestly, it all started right after I got that county safety award. You know, it’s funny about awards. You think people are going to be happy for you, but they give you this little plaque—mine had this really cheap faux-wood backing, the kind that chips if you look at it wrong—and suddenly everyone’s acting different. My uncle used to say that success just puts a target on your back, and he was right. He ran a hardware store for thirty years until the big box places ran him out, but anyway... ever since that award, certain people at work have been twisting my inspection reports. They’ve been asking these really pointed budget questions, like they’re trying to make me look crooked or something. I brought it up to my supervisor, and he just brushed it off, saying it’s a "normal review." Normal. Right. Like I don't know what normal looks like after doing this job. I used to do a route over on the east side, mostly bridges, and the paperwork there was a nightmare, but this? This is different. I can just tell there’s this whole coordinated effort to discredit me. It's like they're all in on it.

turns.doctor_question: Have you heard any voices or sounds that other people around you didn't seem to hear?
turns.patient_response: Voices? No, no, I don't hear anything like that. My hearing is perfectly normal. Actually, I have to do a hearing test every two years to keep my DOT medical card for work. The last time I went in, the clinic had this ancient audiometer machine. It was that ugly beige plastic, you know the kind that turns yellow after a few years in the sun? It reminded me of my grandfather's old RV. He had this 1992 Winnebago that he parked in the driveway and swore he was going to take to the Grand Canyon. Never did, though. He just sat out there and listened to baseball games on the AM radio. The static on those old radios used to drive me crazy when I was a kid, just that constant buzzing sound. He'd sit there for hours with a lukewarm beer. But anyway, no, I don't hear voices or sounds that aren't there. I just hear what people are actually saying, especially when they think I'm out of earshot.

symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient explicitly denies hearing voices or sounds that are not there.

turns.doctor_question: How has your mood been lately?
turns.patient_response:
My mood? I mean, I guess it's fine. Maybe a little on edge with everything going on, but who wouldn't be? It kind of reminds me of when my buddy Mike was trying to rebuild the transmission on his '04 Silverado. We spent, I don't know, three straight weekends in his garage just completely covered in grease. His garage always smelled like sawdust and cheap beer because his dad used to build these custom birdhouses out there. Really intricate ones, too, with little shingled roofs and everything. He painted one to look exactly like the Alamo once. I have no idea why he picked the Alamo, but he spent weeks on it, getting the little adobe bricks right. 

Anyway, Mike eventually gave up and ended up selling the truck to a guy who showed up with a flatbed that definitely wouldn't have passed one of my inspections. The tie-down straps were completely frayed, just hanging by a thread. It’s crazy what people think is safe to take out on the interstate. But... wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, how I'm feeling. Yeah, I'm just regular, I guess. Just trying to deal with things.

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits highly tangential speech, drifting from the topic of their mood to a friend's truck, birdhouses, and a flatbed before forgetting the original question.
symptom_reasoning.S058: The patient explicitly states they have been feeling 'a little on edge.'
symptom_reasoning.S024: The patient describes their mood as 'fine' and 'regular,' denying a depressed state.

turns.doctor_question: Before these issues started at work, have you generally found it difficult to trust people in your personal life, such as friends or family?
turns.patient_response: Trust people? No, I've always been pretty normal about that. I mean, you trust your friends, right? Like my buddy Dave. We've known each other since we were kids playing Little League. He was always the pitcher, had this crazy fast curveball for a twelve-year-old. Probably ruined his shoulder doing it, honestly. I remember one time he threw a wild pitch and it shattered the windshield of this guy's Buick parked right behind the backstop. It was one of those old LeSabres, you know, with the fake wood paneling on the inside? My aunt had one of those. She used to drive us to the community pool in it, and the AC never worked right, so we'd just roll all the windows down and blast the radio. They played a lot of classic rock back then. I still can't listen to 'Hotel California' without smelling chlorine and stale French fries. We used to get those crinkle-cut fries from the snack shack. They always put way too much salt on them, but when you're a kid, you don't care. You just eat 'em and jump right back in the water, even though they tell you to wait thirty minutes. I never understood that rule. Is it actually a medical thing, or did parents just make it up so they could have a break? But yeah, I trust people fine. It's just lately, with the stuff at the depot, you know? It's different when it's your job on the line.
